title: Chirped Thickness-Modulated Stack for Broadband Visible Rejection
scientific_hypothesis: A chirped stack with systematically varying layer thicknesses across 24 layers will achieve broader visible stopband coverage than a periodic stack while maintaining telecom transmittance, because thickness grading extends the effective stopband width.
design_principle: Varying the optical thickness of successive pairs shifts the local Bragg condition, creating overlapping stopbands that merge into a wider composite rejection band; this is the principle behind thickness-modulated designs in L04.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (24 layers, 12 pairs)
design_variables: Thickness progression pattern across the 24 layers
Base center wavelength for the chirp sequence
soft_objectives: Maximize mean reflectance across full 400-700 nm band
Maintain transmittance above threshold in 1530-1565 nm band
Minimize ripple in telecom transmission band
manufacturing_considerations: 24 layers uses 80 percent of the 30-layer budget, leaving margin for future refinement
Thickness variation must remain within deposition tool capability
HfO2/SiO2 system has demonstrated durability in space environments per L03, L15
theory_basis: Chirped Bragg reflector theory for broadband stopbands
expected_advantages: Broader visible stopband than periodic stack
Can tailor transition region between visible and telecom bands
known_risks: More complex optimization landscape with more local minima
May require more iterations to converge
Thickness extremes could approach manufacturability limits
execution_request_english: Design a 24-layer chirped stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: alternating HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) starting with HfO2 (12 pairs total). Optimize layer thicknesses with a chirp constraint where thickness varies systematically from layer 1 to layer 24. Initial thicknesses follow a linear chirp from quarter-wave at 450 nm (first pair) to quarter-wave at 650 nm (last pair). Materials: hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) from catalog. Substrate: SiO2 (Lemarchand) (fused silica). Incident medium: air. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Optimize for maximum reflectance in 400-700 nm and maximum transmittance in 1530-1565 nm.
